RequestHeader.description: Object defining attributes of an insurance service request header

rqUID.description: Unique identifier for client request. UUID format. Used for tracking unique client requests to API. Client app sends identifier which will be echoed back to client in response. If not provided, identifier will be generated for client request. Max 36 characters.

correlationId.description:
Unique identifier for correlating transactions. Recommended in UUID format but not required. Used for tracking transactions across multiple systems. Client app sends identifier which will be echoed back to client in response. Max 36 characters.
Note. This is considered a non-standard attribute available for legacy system usage.

transactionRequestTs.description: Timestamp of request transaction. ISO 8601 date format, YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss[.mmm]TZD. Client app sends transaction timestamp which will be echoed back to client in response. If not provided, timestamp will be generated for client request.

The categorization of property at a residence location based on certain characteristics that affect its insurance coverage.
### Upgraded
* Synthetic, simple wood, veneer, or stucco siding * Basic roof shape and roof cover (asphalt, metal) * Ceramic tile, carpet, or veneer hardwood floors * Standard kitchen and bathroom cabinetry * Minimal upgrades: fireplace, single staircase, one-or-two-car garage

* Exterior finishes indicate architect/designer involvement * Architectural asphalt or wood shingle, slate, or clay tile roof * Kitchen with custom cabinetry and high-end appliances * Typical upgrades: Audio visual, specialty rooms, multiple fireplaces, finished basement

  - For systems using a fire retardant chemical, the fire retardant chemical must meet U.S. Department of Agriculture standards

  - The system must be installed by a licensed contractor in accordance with manufacturer’s specifications.

  - 6d nails @ 6/12/Other - Roof deck is attached with shorter 6d (2.5 inch long) nails spaced at 6 inches along the edge of the sheathing and 12 inches in the interior of the sheathing
  - 8d nails @ 6/12 - Roof deck is attached with 8d (2.5 inch long) nails spaced at 6 inches along the edge of the sheathing and 12 inches in the interior of the sheathing
  - 8d nails @ 6/6 - Roof deck is attached with 8d (2.5 inch long) nails spaced at 6 inches along the edge of the sheathing and the interior of the sheathing. This pattern is seen mostly in newer structures built to high wind standards.
  - Dimensional Lumber 8d nails @ 6/6 - Dimensional lumber or tongue and groove are usually 4 to 8 inch wide boards that are nominally 1 inch thick (3/4 inch actual thickness) and are laid in a fashion that is parallel to the ridge or diagonal to the ridge

wrcBracedRoofCredit.description: A value indicating if the roof of a residence location must be double sloped, attached to trusses and have a gable end that exceeds 50% of a major wall length and each end appears as an inverted V

wrcHipRoofCredit.description: A value indicating if the roof of a residence location must be hip in shape and have no gables that exceeds 50% of a major wall length

wrcRoofToWallConnectionCredit.description:
A value indicating if toenail, clips, single straps, and double straps installed in compliance with the 2006 or subsequent edition of the IRC or an engineered design for the wind speed for at a residence location.
Definitions of Roof-to-Wall connections that qualify
  - Toe Nails/Other - This refers to nails or screws driven at an angle through the truss into the top plate of the wall
  - Clips - This refers to steel straps that attach to the side of the truss. This option also applies if the trusses on the residence are bolted to the top plate of the wall.
  - Single Wraps - This refers to steel straps that wrap over the top of the truss and attach to the wall on one side of the truss only
  - Double Wraps - This refers to steel straps that wrap over the top of the truss and attach to the wall on one side of the truss only

wrcWaterResistanceCredit.description: A value indicating if roofing felt or other approved layer of protection is between the shingles and the roof sheathing below. The structure has self-adhering modified bitumen tape or a foamed polyurethane structural adhesive applied from the inside in order to prevent rain from entering the building in the event that the roof covering fails. S.W.R. must be applied to all spaces between pieces of the roof deck, and must be applied per the manufacturers specifications.
